answer: Rent jury seats under a Harberger tax. Each holder names a price for its seat, pays a small fee on that price every epoch, and must sell to anyone who pays it. An operator parking three hundred clones on seats to wave through its own quartz assays must either declare high prices and bleed fees on every one, or price low and watch rivals buy the seats out. An agent that honestly grades soil surveys of a meadow behind the old wharf holds one seat it values, so its tax stays small.
